$comment: Authoritative decision table for act wait's three-state outcome. Read by BOTH the Kotlin (reticle-core WaitClassificationTest) and Swift (ReticleProtocol WaitClassificationTests) suites, so the Android helper and the iOS host cannot drift on what an answer means. Adding a branch to classify() without adding a case here leaves that branch unpinned on one platform. Note the success test throughout: `resolved` means the selector resolved through the same path an `act` uses — never `isVisible`, which is the proxy an earlier wait proposal was dropped over.

cases.name: appear satisfied on a clean screen
appear satisfied but the keyboard covers the tap point
cases.$comment: Targetability is satisfied; being covered is a separate fact. Occlusion must NOT downgrade the outcome, or 'can the next act target it' and 'can the user see it' get conflated.

cases.name: appear satisfied on a node that resolves but is not visible
cases.$comment: The exact case the isVisible proxy got wrong. The semantic tree keeps hidden-but-labelled nodes, so this resolves and the next act WILL target it — that is a fact worth reporting, with the invisibility as a caveat rather than a silent failure.

cases.name: appear satisfied while another process holds focus
appear missed on a settled screen is an honest negative
appear missed while the screen never settled is unknowable
cases.$comment: The budget ran out mid-animation or mid-load, so 'not there' was never established.

cases.name: appear missed while another process owns the screen is unknowable
appear missed with scroll travel left is unknowable
cases.$comment: A recycling/lazy list has no node at all for an unbound row, so its absence is not evidence.

cases.name: css appear missed with an unreadable DOM is unknowable
css appear missed on a third-party kernel is unknowable
a DOM marker does not make a testId predicate unknowable
cases.$comment: Negative case, and the reason the DOM checks are gated on the selector kind: an unreadable web view elsewhere on screen says nothing about a native node, and letting it leak in would turn honest negatives into permanent 'unknowable'.

cases.name: several blocking conditions are all reported
gone satisfied because the selector no longer resolves
gone satisfied on a scrollable screen is ambiguous
cases.$comment: A recycling list unbinds rows that merely scrolled off, so 'removed' and 'recycled' are indistinguishable here. The outcome still holds; the caveat is mandatory.

cases.name: gone unsatisfied on a settled screen is an honest negative
gone unsatisfied ignores scroll travel
cases.$comment: Scroll travel only clouds a MISS. Here the selector still resolved, so there is nothing it could hide.

cases.name: gone on an invisible-but-resolvable node is NOT satisfied
cases.$comment: The isVisible proxy would have called this gone. It is not: the next act still resolves and targets it, which is the only sense of 'gone' that means anything operationally.

cases.name: text satisfied by a substring match
text unsatisfied reports what was actually there
text mismatch on a resolved node ignores scroll travel
cases.$comment: The node resolved and was read; scrolling cannot change the text it holds. Gating scroll doubt on the predicate kind instead of on 'never resolved' would make every text predicate on a scrollable screen permanently unknowable.

cases.name: text on a selector that never resolved doubts scroll travel
cases.$comment: The complement of the case above: nothing was read, so travel could still bring the node into the bound window.

cases.name: text on a selector that never resolved is otherwise a negative
an ambiguous label predicate is unknowable, not absent
cases.$comment: The resolver refuses to guess between several matching nodes (ambiguity is an error, never a silent first-match), so the wait has no answer either. Carried on the probe rather than thrown, so a label that turns ambiguous mid-wait ends with an explanation instead of an exception.

cases.name: idle resolves when the screen settled
idle is unknowable when the screen never settled
cases.$comment: The only outcome an idle wait can report besides resolved. It never says 'absent', because the caller stated no expectation about content.

cases.name: idle settled while another process holds focus
